cards.explanation: The big thing is that a great number of Jews and Greeks believe. Verse 1 says Paul and Barnabas spoke so well that “…a great number of Jews and Greeks believed.” Not a few. A GREAT number. I've baked batches where three people showed up for cookies, so this one has me jealous.

The answer is False. Verse 3 says they “…spent considerable time there, speaking boldly for the Lord…” Minds were getting poisoned, and these two stayed put and kept speaking. If somebody was bad-mouthing my cookies around town, I'd be hiding under the counter.

The Lord backs up the message by enabling them to perform signs and wonders. Verse 3 says He “…affirmed the message of His grace by enabling them to perform signs and wonders.” The credit goes to Him, not to the two men. Paul and Barnabas carried the message, and the Lord backed it up.

They flee to Lystra and Derbe. Verse 6 says they found out about the plan and fled to “…the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe…” They also went to the surrounding region. When you hear about a stoning plan, you pack fast.

The answer is True. Verse 7 says that in Lystra and Derbe and the surrounding region, “…they continued to preach the gospel.” Run out of one town, and they keep right on preaching in the next. That's not a quitter's schedule.

The word is faith. Verse 9 says Paul looked intently at the man and “…saw that he had faith to be healed.” The man was listening to Paul's words when that happened. I think those words stuck in his heart.
The man jumps up and begins to walk. Verse 10 says, “And the man jumped up and began to walk.” This man had been lame from birth and had never walked. JUMPED. Not crept, not wobbled. Jumped.
They call Barnabas Zeus, friends. Verse 12 says so, and Zeus is a Greek god. The priest of Zeus even had a temple just outside the city (verse 13). That's a big promotion for a traveling preacher.
The word is speaker. Verse 12 says they called Paul Hermes “…because he was the chief speaker.” So the crowd named him for his talking. I've been called plenty for talking too much, but never Hermes.

The priest hopes to offer a sacrifice along with the crowds. Verse 13 says he brought bulls and wreaths to the city gates, “…hoping to offer a sacrifice along with the crowds.” This was a real plan, with real bulls. Bulls and wreaths at the city gates means somebody was serious.

The answer is True, friends. Verse 14 says when the apostles Barnabas and Paul found out, “…they tore their clothes and rushed into the crowd, shouting…” They tore their clothes and rushed into the crowd. That's the text's own picture.

The word is worthless. Verse 15 says to “…turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made heaven and earth and sea and everything in them.” They set the worthless things next to the living God. That's a very short list of choices.

They point to rain from heaven and fruitful seasons. Verse 17 says, “He gives you rain from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.” That's the testimony they point to. Rain on the field, food on the table, gladness in the heart.

The answer is False. Verse 18 says even with these words, Paul and Barnabas “…could hardly stop the crowds from sacrificing to them.” They gave their whole speech and it was still a struggle. That's a tough crowd.

The answer is True. Verse 19 says they stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, “…presuming he was dead.” This is a heavy moment, friends, and I think it hurts to read. I'll stay quiet here and let the verse say it.

Paul gets up and goes back into the city. Verse 20 says that after the disciples had gathered around him, “…he got up and went back into the city.” The next day he left with Barnabas for Derbe. I think those disciples had a lot of feelings in that moment.
They make many disciples. Verse 21 says they preached the gospel to that city and “…made many disciples.” After all they'd been through, this is good news. Many disciples in Derbe, friends.
The answer is False. Verse 21 says they “…returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch…” These were the towns where things got rough. They went back.

They strengthen the disciples and urge them to keep the faith. Verse 22 says they were “…strengthening the souls of the disciples and encouraging them to continue in the faith.” They came back to those disciples with encouragement. That's good friends right there.

The word is hardships. Verse 22 says, “We must endure many hardships to enter the kingdom of God…” They said it to the disciples they were encouraging. Paul and Barnabas had just lived hard days themselves.

They appoint elders. Verse 23 says Paul and Barnabas “…appointed elders for them in each church…” So every church got leaders before the two moved on. Good baking, good teams, and no one left holding the oven mitts alone.

The answer is True. Verse 23 says they appointed elders in each church, “…praying and fasting as they entrusted them to the Lord, in whom they had believed.” So they prayed and they fasted while they appointed elders. They did it with the Lord in mind.

The place is Attalia, friends. Verse 25 says that when they had spoken the word in Perga, “…they went down to Attalia.” Verse 26 says they sailed from there to Antioch. Attalia is the last stop before the boat.

They report all that God had done through them. Verse 27 says they gathered the church together and “…reported all that God had done through them…” Notice who gets the credit. God did it through them.
The word is Gentiles. Verse 27 says God “…opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.” Gentiles means people who weren't Jews. God opened that door, and that's what Paul and Barnabas reported.
